item.title: Most common players on eliminated teams from Week 9 in Yahoo Fantasy Death leagues — plus FAB waiver wire advice
item.description: Every week I'll examine the most common NFL players on the teams eliminated in Yahoo Death Leagues, trying to figure out where the puck is headed. I will also offer some FAB advice ($1,000 cap is the Yahoo default), but please remember this area is highly context-sensitive and manager-specific. Waiver strategy in Death Leagues I like to trust myself (and my depth) in the early weeks, and take heart that it's not that difficult to beat just one team when a Death League is still large. As such, I'm not proactive on early offers. I'm definitely more proactive now, but remember that the strength of each cut team becomes much stronger as we get deep into the season. Be very careful not to drain your remaining budget for the future. Death Leagues are back and better than ever. (Photo by Grant Thomas/Yahoo Sports) Understanding FAB recommendations I'll offer bidding in three buckets, and you'll need to season the recommendations to taste. You know your context and league habits better than an outsider would. But just know the immediacy has stepped up a bit. I still think it's a mistake to spend all of your money in the present — the wire gets stronger and stronger in every passing week — but I also understand the gravity at hand. So don't be afraid to get in there with some competitive offers. My weekly FAB recommendations will come in three buckets: Proactive : This means you highly covet this player, perhaps might even need this player. I realize these offers might not win if someone in your league is lighting money on fire, but as described above, that's often a short-sighted mistake in this format. Reactive : This means you desire the player but the offer has to make sense for your short- or long-term strategy. Keep Them Honest : This is an offer that is not designed to win, but might surprisingly land a player if your opponents are distracted by other talent available or unexpectedly passive that week. I often compare notes with other experienced Death League players and we're surprised at how often the Keep Them Honest offers actually win (this is also a portable strategy for regular season-long leagues; you never know when strange market behavior will come about). One last note : Understand that the FAB recommendations are with the assumption that you won't be making offers for every available player. Week 9's top-10 players on eliminated teams 1. WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seahawks (25.6%) JSN had just his second off game of the year, a WR34 finish against the Cardinals. It was still a seven-catch, 10-target day, which illustrates the solid floor here, even if Drew Lock is playing. Pay up. FAB Recommendation: $325 proactive $185 reactive $100 keep them honest 2. RB D’Andre Swift, Bears (21.3%) Tampa Bay’s nasty run defense was staunch all night, and a bunch of Chicago turnovers kept the Bears under their point projection. Swift remains a steady option forward, but he can’t help you during a Week 10 bye. FAB Recommendation: $130 proactive $65 reactiv

item.title: The Washington Wizards Finally Have a Reason to Believe
item.description: Over the past few years, the Washington Wizards haven’t given fans much reason to believe a playoff run is within reach. Since Bradley Beal was traded in 2023, the franchise has been rebuilding, struggling to win and sitting near the bottom of the Eastern Conference. But this year gives fans hope. The Wizards might not finish near the top of the Eastern Conference standings, but they have the talent to compete at a level fans haven’t seen in years. As of right now, the Wizards would make the play-in tournament , something they haven’t done since 2021. In fact, they haven’t played any postseason basketball since then . Washington Has Built Something Real Unlike recent years , this Wizards roster combines veteran experience with young talent. The Wizards have already begun building a foundation of young talent through drafts. In 2023, they acquired Bilal Coulibaly ’s draft rights from the Indiana Pacers. A year later, they selected Alex Sarr and acquired Kyshawn George ’s draft rights from the New York Knicks. However, the most significant changes came last season. On Jan. 9, 2026, the Wizards acquired Trae Young from the Atlanta Hawks. Then, on Feb. 5, they added veteran big man Anthony Davis in a deal with the Dallas Mavericks. Despite finishing 17-65, the Wizards had another reason to be optimistic. They won the 2026 NBA Draft Lottery on May 10, securing the first overall pick, which they used to select BYU star AJ Dybantsa on June 23. Of course, having talented players on paper doesn’t guarantee success. But this combination gives Washington the foundation it needs to become competitive after years of struggling. The Early Results Are Encouraging Right now, the Wizards are 4-7, sitting 10th in the Eastern Conference. While it’s still early in the season, there’s reason to be encouraged by what has been seen so far. Washington has already picked up wins against Milwaukee, Chicago, Charlotte and Orlando, showing that it can compete with different types of opponents. One of the biggest positives has been Trae Young ‘s ability to get his teammates involved. Through 11 games, Young is averaging 18.4 points and 8.9 assists per game. He’s already shown that he can be the primary playmaker this team needs, consistently creating opportunities for teammates while remaining a scoring threat himself. AJ Dybantsa has also been impressive early in his rookie season. Through his first four games, he averaged 16.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists while shooting 46.2% from the field. He’s already shown flashes of his scoring ability, including a 21-point performance against Orlando on Nov. 2. There will naturally be growing pains as Dybantsa adjusts to the NBA, but his early production is encouraging. Trae Young Gives Washington an Offensive Engine It Hasn’t Had in Years Although the Wizards have made several moves to reshape the organization, acquiring Young was the most important one. item.title: Ryan Day plans to start Ohio State QB Luke Fahey vs Northwestern
item.description: Ohio State will start freshman quarterback Luke Fahey against Northwestern on Nov. 14, coach Ryan Day said Nov. 10. It will be Fahey's third consecutive start. Fahey was elevated to the starting role after Julian Sayin sustained an injury in Ohio State's win against Indiana. With the injury unspecified, there is no timeline for Sayin's return. More on Luke Fahey: Grading QB Luke Fahey in Ohio State football 41-28 loss to Oregon "Luke [Fahey] is going to be our quarterback this week, and Tavien [St. Clair] is one snap away," Day said. "... If we feel like [St. Clair] gives us the best chance to win, we'll make that move, but we're not at that point right now." Fahey started during Ohio State's consecutive losses to USC and Oregon. It's the first time the Buckeyes have dropped back-to-back regular-season wins since 2011. In those games, Fahey has 620 passing yards, three touchdowns and an interception on a 64.8% completion rate. Ohio State's offense has been stagnant without Sayin. Against USC, Ohio State struggled to find the end zone and settled for four field goals. Against Oregon, wide receiver Jeremiah Smith went nearly two full quarters without a catch. Ohio State went up 14-0 after the first quarter, but Oregon scored 38 straight points afterward. St. Clair, a former five-star recruit, has not played since Sayin's absence. item.title: Maple Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev sounds pretty pissed about load management plan
item.description: © Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Maple Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev sounds pretty pissed about load management plan appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It has not been the best start to the season for the Toronto Maple Leafs , as they sit in seventh place in the Atlantic Division. Their prize pick-up in free agency, Sergei Bobrovsky, has struggled , as the Leafs have dropped five of their last six games. Two of those losses came at home over the weekend. They were defeated by the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday, 4-2, and then by the New Jersey Devils on Sunday, 4-0. In the game on Sunday, veteran defenseman Chris Tanev was a scratch, a decision Leafs coach Jim Hiller said was part of a plan for load management , according to Terry Koshan of The Toronto Sun. “We’re trying to manage him a little bit,” Hiller said before the game on Sunday. “(He) wants to play every single game, every night. He loves to go, and he was on the ice this morning. I think that’ll probably be part of the plan.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Now, Tanev is responding to the idea of load management , according to Jonas Siegel of The Athletic. “Chris Tanev says he doesn’t agree with the Leafs’ load management plan for him: ‘I want to play.’” Siegel posted on X, formerly Twitter. The idea of Tanev needing load management may be a smart one. While he wants to be on the ice, he has had trouble staying on the ice in recent years. He has already missed time this year due to an upper body injury, playing in just nine of the team’s 19 games so far. Last year, due to a groin injury and core muscle surgery, he played in just 11 games. Tanev has not played a full season since the 2021-22 campaign with the Calgary Flames, when he played all 82 games. He played 75 games in both 2023-24 and 2024-25, but still missed some time with injuries. This year, the production for Tanev has also not been at its peak. He has just one assist in nine games so far for the team. The Maple Leafs return to the ice on Tuesday night against the Colorado Avalanche, with Tanev expected to be playing.

item.title: 'I'm just sick of it': Kane Williamson admits frustration with 'good guy' label attached to him and NZ cricketers
item.description: 'I'm just sick of it': Kane Williamson admits frustration with 'good guy' label attached to him and NZ cricketers originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Kane Williamson says he is tired of the "good guy" label attached to him and New Zealand cricket. He described the dressing room after the 2019 World Cup final as quiet and bewildered. Williamson said people kept approaching him about the final for months afterward. Why Kane Williamson is tired of the good guy tag in New Zealand cricket Kane Williamson has spent the better part of a decade being described as cricket's most agreeable man, a reputation sealed by the way he handled the 2019 World Cup final. Asked about it on Stick to Cricket , he made clear the label has worn thin. Michael Vaughan put it to him that the calm, humble temperament has been a constant in New Zealand sides for as long as he has watched them, and asked whether it is something players are raised into. Williamson's answer suggested the framing itself is the problem. "Humility gets thrown around a lot, I reckon, and often it can probably be acted. But for us, it's just trying to stay authentic," he said. "Even the 'good guy' tag, I'm just sick of it, to be fair. You're just trying to do what you do in a way that makes sense to you." He did accept there may be something broader behind it, pointing to other New Zealand teams rather than to cricket alone. "It probably comes through in some of our other sports teams. Maybe it's just culturally in the country." MORE: 'We actually didn't win the World Cup?': Michael Vaughan jokes as Kane Williamson brings up Ben Stokes incident from 2019 WC final What the New Zealand dressing room was like after the 2019 World Cup final The reason the tag stuck is Lord's. New Zealand tied the final, tied the Super Over and lost on boundary countback, and Williamson's response in the aftermath was widely praised as gracious at a moment when nobody would have blamed him for anything else. His description of that night was less about grace than about confusion. "It was quiet, a few beers, and every five minutes, you know, 'What the hell just happened there?' And then you kind of crack on and go back to that thought," Williamson said. Phil Tufnell told him the reaction from the team had been remarkable and admitted he would have been furious in their position. Williamson's explanation was that distance made it worse rather than better. "The final experience was tough. Probably afterwards, in the months following it, you were actually sort of bumping into people constantly, and they'd watched it and just lived through it. It was massive," he said. "But you have a little less emotion when you're directly involved." item.title: Xavier v. Detroit Mercy: Preview, matchups, and keys to the game
item.description: Detroit Mercy Titans forward London Maiden (20) pushes past Wright State Raiders forward Michael Imariagbe (33) on Tuesday, March 10, 2026, at Corteva Coliseum at the Indiana State Fairgrounds in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There is a limited amount of information that can reliably be garnered from the amount of games played at this point in the season, and it’s questionable whether or not that information will be accurate or even pertinent when March rolls around. A lot can change during the course of a college basketball campaign, and both attrition and development will change the composition and performance of virtually every roster during that time. Those disclaimers should serve as context when I tell you that Detroit Mercy is not a good team and this game will serve only as a counting stat in the Q4 column when resume time rolls around. Fresh off of a season in which they won just a single non-conference game against D1 competition, UDM lost by 61 to Marquette in their season opener on Friday. They peaked at 1.2% win probability by trailing just 9-8 before surrendering a 10-0 run in just over two minutes of game time. A 36-5 run that straddled the half functionally ended the game, as 36-5 runs tend to do. Pick a stat and it looks bad for them, but maybe the most notable is that they scored in just 6 of their 34 second half possessions. It was a destruction. Xavier, on the other hand, has been gorging on cupcakes. The Muskies brushed aside Mount St. Mary’s in the opener and then outscored Eastern Michigan 65-35 after the second media timeout of the game to turn a slow start into a comfortable victory. Sterner tests lie ahead, but for the moment, X has been giving it to all takers while barely breaking a sweat. Team fingerprint As might be expected of a team that lost by 60, the numbers aren’t pretty for Detroit Mercy. They’re a merely bad offensive rebounding team; the rest of the offensive side of the ledger is absolutely abysmal. They’re in the bottom 10 of D1 in free throw rate, turnover rate, and EFG% as a team. They can’t hit from inside or beyond the arc, and they’re poor from the line. They had almost a quarter of their two-point shots blocked and played at a glacial pace. Just ugly ball. Defensively, it’s not as bad, but it’s still not good. They managed to keep Marquette off the line, though that appears to be through a lack of meaningful resistance rather than any real defensive nous. They somehow forced just 3 turnovers in a 67 possession game, which is honestly incredible. The rest of the numbers are also bad, but again, it’s a one game sample. I think the biggest takeaway is that Marquette destroyed them and, if Xavier wants to compete near the top of the Big East this year, they need to do the same. item.title: Boston Half winner Habtom Samuel withdraws from 2026 Manchester Road Race
item.description: A file photo of the Manchester Road Race. (Courtesy of Rick Dyer) MANCHESTER - Boston Half marathon winner Habtom Samuel announced Monday night that he will not be running in this year's Manchester Road Race due to fatigue. Samuel, who won the Boston Half marathon Nov. 8, had committed to running in the annual Thanksgiving Day race in Connecticut on Sept. 9, according to a news release from the Manchester Road Race Committee. Race officials announced his entry alongside a lineup of other elite athletes and former Manchester Road Race winners in a media release Monday. However, Samuel's manager informed the race in an email Monday night that Samuel was withdrawing from the race due to "fatigue from such a long competitive season," according to the race committee's release. "We are disappointed, but hopefully Habtom will compete in Manchester in the future," said Jim Harvey, the Manchester Road Race's elite runner coordinator. "We still have an exceptional elite field and it will be another great race this year." Harvey announced Monday that this year's race participants will include 2025 men's division winner Edwin Kurgat , 2025 runner-up Dave Mullarkey and World Champion Dawit Seare. They will be joined at the Main Street starting line by 2023 Manchester Road Race winner Morgan Beadlescomb and two-time Manchester Road Race champion and Olympic silver medalist Sally Kipyego. Presented by Hartford HealthCare and organized by more than 400 volunteers, the annual Manchester Road Race will be held Thanksgiving Day at 10 a.m. The race will be held on a 4.737-mile loop through the central streets of Manchester, starting and finishing on Main Street in front of St. James Church. Registration is available online for $40, and then will increase to $42 on Nov. 21. Participants unable to make it to Manchester on Thanksgiving Day can sign up for the race's virtual option, according to Danie Kennedy, registrar and executive board member of the Manchester Road Race Committee. Participants can register for the online option for $30 and download the race app to track their progress, Kennedy said. All registration will close at 11:59 p.m. Nov. 24, Kennedy said. Main Street will close at 5:30 a.m. the day of the race and remain closed until 11:30 a.m., according to the event's website. All roads intersecting the racecourse as well as exit ramps from Interstate 384 will be closed at 9 a.m., with normal traffic resuming after 11:30 a.m., the website said. All proceeds from this year's race will be split between Rebuilding Together of Manchester and Habitat for Humanity of North Central Connecticut . For more information, visit the Manchester Road Race website. This story includes prior Hearst Media Connecticut reporting. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. item.title: Arsenal plot January swoop for 20-year-old Real Madrid attacker – report
item.description: Arsenal plot January swoop for 20-year-old Real Madrid attacker – report In a major development, talkSPORT reports that Arsenal have set their sights on a potential January move for Real Madrid young forward Endrick. The 20-year-old Brazilian attacker has found minutes hard to come by this season and the Gunners are looking to capitalise on his situation and offer him a way out. Arsenal want Endrick It has been another difficult start to the season for Endrick as he missed the early parts of the campaign with an injury sustained during pre-season. Upon returning, the former Palmeiras wonderkid has found his role pretty much non-existent as the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Yan Diomande, Arda Guler, Vinicius Jr., Carlos Espi, and Brahim Diaz are all ahead of him in manager Jose Mourinho’s order of preference. It has restricted Endrick to only a total of 141 minutes of game-time across seven matches in all competitions, in which he has scored and assisted one goal apiece. Arsenal interested in Endrick. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Given the circumstances, talk of another loan exit in January, like last season, has been speculated, even though Mourinho has shut down those rumours multiple times. Now, Arsenal have said to be weighing up a move for Endrick. Following the injury to Bukayo Saka, Mikel Arteta & co. are on the lookout for a forward who can come in and make an impact. While their priority remains Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi, the Frenchman is not for sale, forcing the Gunners to assess alternatives, leading to Endrick. Arsenal director Andrea Berta has a good relationship with the Brazilian’s representatives, who had already offered the youngster to the club last January. What has Endrick said? However, in a recent interview, Endrick made it clear that he is not thinking about leaving Real Madrid and that he remains fully committed to the club and manager Mourinho. Will Endrick stay or leave? (Photo by Albert Perez/Getty Images) “I have a lot of faith in Mourinho. Every single day, he checks in on me—not to talk about football, but to ask about my personal life,” he said . “I will always give everything for Real Madrid as the club comes before anyone else, but with the care and affection Mourinho shows me, I’m even more motivated to give my all.” Despite the youngster’s statements, reliable journalist Matteo Moretto has reported that there is a 70% chance of Endrick leaving on loan , with multiple Premier League clubs and Serie A sides interested. Only time will tell if the interest shown from Arsenal materialises into something substantial in the weeks to come.

item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Heat vs. Jazz injury report: Are Giannis Antetokounmpo, Lauri Markkanen playing? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat could have Giannis Antetokounmpo available for Tuesday night’s matchup against the Utah Jazz , while Lauri Markkanen’s status remains uncertain as both stars deal with right wrist sprains. According to the NBA’s Tuesday morning injury report, Antetokounmpo is listed as probable, while Markkanen is questionable. Miami (4-6) will conclude its shaky five-game road trip against Utah (1-9) , which enters the contest on an eight-game losing streak. Tipoff is scheduled for 9 p.m. ET. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Antetokounmpo’s probable designation suggests he is expected to play, although his availability has not been officially confirmed. Through 10 games this season, the two-time MVP is averaging 27.5 points, 12.8 rebounds and 5.3 assists while shooting 56.6% from the field. The Heat are coming off a 114-108 victory over the Sacramento Kings on Sunday, with Antetokounmpo recording 29 points, 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks while shooting 14-for-23 from the field. Klay Thompson also contributed 23 points, connecting on seven 3-pointers to help Miami secure its fourth victory of the season. Giannis Antetokounmpo, Lauri Markkanen injuries raise questions ahead of Heat-Jazz clash Tom Horak-Imagn Images Meanwhile, Markkanen’s potential absence would further complicate matters for a Utah team struggling to generate victories early in the season. The Jazz will also be without Keyonte George (right ankle sprain), Jaren Jackson Jr. (right MCL tear) and Jusuf Nurkic (right second plantar plate tear). Additionally, Trey Alexander, Kobe Bufkin and Harrison Ingram have been ruled out because of G League two-way assignments. Utah’s depleted rotation presents another challenge as the organization attempts to snap its eight-game losing streak. Both teams will continue monitoring their injured stars ahead of Tuesday’s matchup, with their final availability expected to become clearer closer to tipoff. item.title: Australian Jockey Izzy Neale Dead at 22 After Being Thrown From Her Horse
item.description: Newscom/MEGA Australian apprentice jockey Izzy Neale has died after an incident that took place over the weekend in New South Wales. She was 22. Reuters reported on Tuesday, November 10, that she was thrown from her horse, Marnoo, during the Warren Shire Cotton Cup on Sunday, November 8, and airlifted to Dubbo hospital. “It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends,” read a statement from the family posted on the official Racing NSW X account . “Izzy rode horses before she could walk,” the statement continued. “Her love of horses was a lifelong passion that, more recently, had grown into a love of racing.” Noting that Izzy’s organs will be donated, the family said she will “give others the chance of life, bringing some comfort to our family amid this devastating loss.” The family thanked their relatives, friends and the racing community as well as Racing NSW, the NSW Jockeys Association and “the medical staff who cared for Izzy with such compassion” for their support. “As we come to terms with our loss, we ask that our family’s privacy be respected,” the statement concluded. “Izzy was dearly loved and will forever be in our hearts.” Newscom/MEGA According to the New York Post , Izzy “lost consciousness” after she was dislodged from her horse at about the 400-meter mark during the Warren Shire Cotton Cup. She was reportedly placed on life support after being taken to the hospital. Per the Post , the final race of the program was abandoned, and Marnoo was euthanized. Thoroughbred Daily News reported that jockey Diego Montes de Oca was also dislodged from his horse and suffered a foot injury. According to the outlet, Izzy’s death is the first racing fatality in New South Wales since Darren Jones died in April 2017. Izzy’s brother Tommy Neale wrote on Facebook that he couldn’t “believe what’s happened,” adding: “You’ll always be my lil baby sister, you were my best friend an we always was so close so I dunno how I’m gonna deal with this.” “I’m so sorry I spent years in jail and didn’t spend much time together before this accident,” he added. “I can’t even comprehend how I feel till we meet again sis ❤ gonna miss you so much!!” Read More From First for Sports Josh Allen Goes Viral for Avoiding Eye Contact With Attractive Female Reporter During Postgame Interview Tony Romo Returns to Football Commentary in Unexpected Appearance for First Time Since CBS Departure Arnold Schwarzenegger’s Son Makes Successful ‘Pro Debut’ in Natural Bodybuilding Competition This story Australian Jockey Izzy Neale Dead at 22 After Being Thrown From Her Horse first appeared on First for Sports . item.description: LEXINGTON, KY - NOVEMBER 06: Kentucky Wildcats associate coach Mark Fox talks with Kentucky Wildcats forward Milan Momcilovic (22) in a game between the James Madison Dukes and the Kentucky Wildcats on November 6, 2026, at Rupp Arena in Lexington, KY. (Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s a college basketball heavyweight clash tonight, as the Jayhawks travel to the Chicago to take on Kentucky in the yearly Champions Classic. Both teams have 2-0 records after taking care of business in their opening tune-ups, but each team is being truly tested for the first time tonight. With dangerous perimeter threats like Milan Momcilovic (formerly of the Iowa State Hawkeyes), and some legitimate athletes, Kansas will need to dictate the tempo, wall off transition opportunities, and establish control in the half-court, and hopefully running an effective half court offense, something that’s been lacking in recent years under Self. Coach Mark Pope likes to assemble teams that can spread the floor and shoot. However, fans of BBN have been underwhelmed by the talent he’s been able to assemble in Lexington so far. Kentucky comes in ranked just 35th by Bart Torvik, largely based on preseason inputs, with the 26th ranked offense and 55th ranked defense. The Wildcats don’t currently look like a team that will force a lot of turnovers, which is good given Melvin Council’s absence and reliance in Taylen Kinney. They do look to be a solid offensive rebounding team so far, so Self will need to keep that in mind as he continues tinkering with the frontcourt configurations early in the season. Ultimately I think it’s pretty clear that Kansas has an overall talent and athleticism advantage, but Kentucky will shoot threes and loo likely shoot them well, which can keep a team in just about any game. Kansas is currently a 4.5 point favorite, and even without Council, that sounds about right to me. I think Kentucky scores more than Self would care to see, but Kansas will establish themselves well enough on both ends to come out on top in a close game. Kansas 79, Kentucky 73

item.title: Breslow Won’t Lock In Story, Leaving Red Sox Shortstop Spot Open
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow refused to name Trevor Story the starting shortstop for next season during Monday’s meetings in Las Vegas. This lack of a firm commitment sends a clear signal to the fanbase that the 34-year-old veteran is not a guaranteed lock. Breslow told reporters that while the team holds “a ton of confidence in Trevor,” final decisions will happen privately between him and the player long before any public announcement, according to the Boston Globe . A sports hernia injury limited Story to 64 games last season, resulting in a .235 average and .621 OPS, which explains the hesitation. Since signing a six-year, $140 million deal before the 2022 season, Story has appeared in just 384 of a possible 810 games. The math simply does not add up for a player on the final year of such a massive contract. Looking at the Bench Options The team is now openly considering other paths to fix the shortstop position. Breslow admitted the organization must be “open-minded about ways to improve the team” after finishing the 2026 season with an 87-75 record. Attention is turning toward minor league standout Franklin Arias, who posted a .957 OPS over 117 games last season. Breslow noted that the club is currently focused on “figuring out his readiness [for the majors] and what the timeline looks like” for the 21-year-old. With Arias finishing the year at Triple-A Worcester, the door is wide open for a younger, healthier option to take the job. A Front Office in Flux Breslow is also trying to rebuild the leadership behind the scenes while making roster decisions. He stated that the “executive leadership circle is down not just bodies, but down really talented people” after losing key assistant GMs Paul Toboni and Taylor Smith, according to Over the Monster . The General Manager role has remained vacant since 2023, adding to the instability. This lack of depth makes finding the right personnel even harder as the team aims to win more games in 2027 than they did in 2026. The front office is prioritizing new hires to fill these gaps before the season begins. With 54 points, rookie Payton Tolle placed third in AL Rookie of the Year voting, indicating bright spots within the team’s rotation. After retaining most of last year’s roster, Breslow characterized the Sox as “opportunistic” in the trade and free agent market.
